mainTopic: Quality rules for wine for נסכים, the end of פרק כל קרבנות הציבור, and the start of the new פרק on the measuring vessels of the מקדש
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about choosing wine for נסכים. The wine is taken from the middle of the barrel, and the גזבר knocks with a reed to stop the flow when scum appears. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says wine with white scum is פסול. The גמרא resolves a contradiction about sweet wine. רבינא combines the clauses into one rule, and רב אשי says sun sweetness is fine but fruit sweetness is not. It then looks for רבי's source for avoiding aged wine and settles on רבא's 'כי יתאדם'. Short ברייתות explain worked vineyards, medium casks, and why the גזבר knocks instead of speaking: speech harms wine. רבי יוחנן's question about lashes for consecrating unfit wine ends in תיקו. After a list of the best animals for קרבנות and an aggadah about the watchmen on ירושלים's walls, the פרק ends. A new פרק opens about the dry measuring vessels in the מקדש, and רבי מאיר's source for two עשרון vessels, one heaped and one leveled.

steps.title: Take the wine from the middle third of the barrel
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its rule: wine for נסכים is taken neither from the top (scum) nor the bottom (dregs), only from the middle third.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Not from the top of the barrel, because of] the flour-like scum, and not from its bottom, because of the dregs. Rather, one brings from its middle third.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing a sentence that began on the previous page. It tells us which part of the barrel the wine for נסכים should come from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two problem zones in a wine barrel. At the top floats a white, flour-like scum (קמחין), and at the bottom the dregs (שמרים) settle. So the משנה says to take the clean wine from the middle third.

keyTerms.meaning: White, flour-like scum that floats on top of wine
Dregs; the sediment that sinks to the bottom of the barrel
Its bottom (the lower part of the barrel)
From its middle third

phrases.english: [not from the top, because of] the flour-like scum,
phrases.notes: This sentence started on the previous page: don't take wine from the top of the barrel, because of this white scum.

phrases.english: and not from its bottom – because of the dregs,
rather, one brings from its middle third.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous page about choosing wine for נסכים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine for נסכים is taken from the middle third of the barrel, avoiding the scum on top and the dregs on the bottom.

steps.title: How the treasurer checks the wine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes how the גזבר makes sure only middle wine is taken: he sits with a reed and knocks when the scum starts coming out.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he check? The treasurer sits with the reed in his hand. When the flow draws out the chalk-like scum, he knocks with the reed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a practical question, how do we know the wine is from the middle, and answers it. The גזבר watches the wine pour out and gives a signal with a reed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wine is let out of the cask through a tap. When the גזבר sees the flow start to carry out chalk-like scum (גיר), he knocks with his reed as a signal to close the tap. In this way only good middle wine is collected.

keyTerms.meaning: Temple treasurer, in charge of supplies like wine
A reed or stick, used here to give a signal
Chalk; here, the chalk-like white scum
He knocked (as a signal)

phrases.english: How does he check?
The treasurer sits, and the reed is in his hand,
when [the flow] throws out the chalk-like scum, he knocks with the reed.
phrases.notes: The knock is a signal to close the tap, so no more scummy wine comes out.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: שאלה / תשובה (the משנה asks and answers its own question)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains in practice how the rule of step 1 (middle third) is carried out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גזבר watches the flow and knocks with a reed to stop it when the scum appears.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: wine with scum is invalid
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה rules that wine with the flour-like scum is פסול, learning from the word תמימים, which covers the offerings, their מנחה, and their נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי, son of רבי יהודה, says: wine that has flour-like scum in it is invalid, as it says: 'Unblemished they shall be for you... and their meal offering... unblemished they shall be for you, and their libations.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא goes further than the first part of the משנה. He says wine with the scum is not just second-best. It is actually פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the משנה only told us where in the barrel to take the wine from. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says scummy wine is disqualified. His proof is that the פסוקים put the word תמימים (unblemished) next to the offerings, their מנחה, and their נסכים, so the wine also must be flawless.

keyTerms.meaning: Invalid; cannot be used for the offering
Unblemished, without any flaw
Their meal offering
Their libations (the wine poured on the מזבח)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the word תמימים, usually said about animals, also applies to the flour and wine that come with them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
[wine] that has flour-like scum in it – is invalid,
as it says: 'Unblemished they shall be for you,' 'and their meal offering,'
'Unblemished they shall be for you, and their libations.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 28:31

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a stricter view to step 1: scum does not only mean you should avoid that wine, it makes the wine פסול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine containing flour-like scum is פסול for נסכים, because offerings, their מנחה, and their נסכים must all be תמימים.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the rule about sweet, boiled and smoked wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by quoting the משנה: sweet, boiled, or smoked wine may not be brought, and if it was brought, it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: One may not bring sweet wine, nor boiled wine, nor smoked wine, and if one brought it, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and quotes a line from the משנה. This is setup. The next step will ask a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted line says these three kinds of wine are not just to be avoided. Even after the fact they are פסול. This detail is exactly what the next step will question.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Sweet (wine)
Boiled or cooked (wine)
Smoked; wine made from grapes dried with smoke

phrases.english: Gemara: One may not bring sweet [wine],
nor boiled, nor smoked,
and if one brought it – it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּמָ׳ אֵין מְבִיאִין לֹא מָתוֹק וְלֹא מְבוּשָּׁל וְלֹא מְעוּשָּׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה to the גמרא by quoting a line from the משנה as the starting point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sweet, boiled, and smoked wine are פסול for נסכים even after the fact.

steps.title: Contradiction: the first clause says sun-dried sweet wine is valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the first part of the משנה says wine from sun-dried grapes is כשר if brought, so how can the later part call sweet wine פסול?
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't the first clause teach: One may not bring sun-dried-grape wine, but if one brought it, it is valid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction between two parts of the same משנה. One sweet wine is כשר after the fact, but the other sweet wine is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הליסטיון is wine made from grapes dried in the sun, which makes it sweet. The רישא says it is כשר if someone brought it, while the later clause says מתוק is פסול. Both are sweet wines, so the גמרא asks why they get different results.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause (earlier part) of the משנה
Sweet wine made from grapes dried in the sun
Valid (after the fact)

steps.confusionAlert: Both clauses start with אין מביאין ('one may not bring'). The difference is only in the ending: one says כשר, the other says פסול. That ending is where the question lies.

phrases.english: But doesn't the first clause teach:
One may not bring sun-dried-grape wine,
but if one brought it – it is valid?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the line quoted in step 4 by setting it against the earlier clause of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that sweet wine (מתוק) is פסול after the fact.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הליסטיון is also sweet wine, and the רישא calls it כשר after the fact. So it seems contradictory for the later clause to call sweet wine פסול.

steps.title: רבינא: Join the two clauses into one rule
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers the contradiction by saying the משנה's two clauses should be joined and taught as one rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Combine the clauses and teach them together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the question from Step 5. He says the משנה's two parts should be joined and read as a single rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction came from one clause calling sun-dried grape wine כשר and another calling sweet wine פסול. רבינא removes the contradiction by fixing the text: all these wines belong in one list and get one ruling. Once there is only one ruling, nothing contradicts.

keyTerms.meaning: Combine and teach: join the two clauses into one statement

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Combine and teach.
phrases.notes: He means: join both parts of the משנה so all these wines get the same ruling, and they are all unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the text of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה gives two different rulings, one כשר and one פסול, and they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The clauses are really one unit with a single ruling, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: רב אשי: Sun sweetness is fine, fruit sweetness is not
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי keeps the משנה as it is. Sweetness that comes from the sun is not disgusting, while sweetness from the fruit itself is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Sweetness that comes from the sun is not disgusting. Sweetness that comes from the fruit is disgusting.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second answer to Step 5. He keeps both clauses and explains why they really are different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grapes dried in the sun get sweet from the sun's heat, and that kind of sweetness is not considered disgusting, so the wine is כשר after the fact. Sweetness that comes from the fruit itself is considered disgusting, so that wine is פסול. Two different sources of sweetness give two different rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: Sweetness
The sun
Disgusting, objectionable

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Sweetness from the sun is not disgusting,
sweetness from the fruit is disgusting.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר חוּלְיָא דְּשִׁימְשָׁא לָא מְאִיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the same קשיא that רבינא answered
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sweet wine is sweet wine, so both clauses should get the same ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: Where the sweetness comes from matters: sun sweetness is acceptable, fruit sweetness is not.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the sweet-wine contradiction. רבינא joins the clauses into one rule. רב אשי splits the cases by where the sweetness comes from: the sun or the fruit.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: Aged wine may not be brought
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. רבי says aged wine may not be brought, and the חכמים allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not bring aged wine; these are the words of רבי. The חכמים allow it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the משנה's argument about old wine. This sets up the search for רבי's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that aged wine should not be used for נסכים. The חכמים say it is fine. The next steps will look for the source of רבי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Old, aged (here: wine more than a year old)
They rule it valid

phrases.english: One may not bring aged wine; these are the words of Rabbi,
and the Sages deem it valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the sweet-wine discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, aged wine may not be brought for נסכים. The חכמים say it is valid.

steps.title: חזקיה: Wine is like the lamb, in its first year
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה gives רבי's source. The פסוק puts 'lamb' next to 'wine', so just as the lamb is in its first year, the wine must be too.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: What is רבי's reason? The פסוק says 'for the lamb, wine'. Just as the lamb is in its first year, the wine must also be in its first year.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה asks for רבי's reason and answers it himself with a פסוק that puts lamb and wine side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the words 'lamb' and 'wine' stand right next to each other, חזקיה compares them. A lamb for a קרבן must be within its first year, so the wine must also be less than a year old. This explains why רבי forbids aged wine.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
In its first year

phrases.english: Chizkiya said:
What is the reason of Rabbi?
The verse states: "for the lamb, wine,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 28:14

phrases.english: just as a lamb is in its first year,
so too the wine must be in its first year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי's ruling in Step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the פסוק puts wine next to the lamb, the wine must be in its first year, just like the lamb.

steps.title: Challenge: Then second-year wine should be totally invalid
steps.stepSummary: If wine is like the lamb, second-year wine should be פסול even after the fact, as a second-year lamb is. But a ברייתא says second-year wine is כשר if already brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as a two-year-old lamb is פסול, two-year-old wine should be פסול! And if you say that is true, a ברייתא teaches: Wine in its second year should not be brought, but if it was brought, it is כשר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks חזקיה's comparison. If you compare fully, old wine should be פסול even after the fact, and a ברייתא says it is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison should work all the way through. A lamb past its first year is completely פסול, so old wine should be completely פסול too. The ברייתא, however, rules 'don't bring it, but if you did, it is כשר', which does not match a lamb.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say that is indeed so
From the start / after the fact (the idea behind 'לא יביא' versus 'אם הביא')

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה כֶּבֶשׂ בֶּן שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים – פָּסוּל,
phrases.english: If so, just as a lamb in its second year is invalid,

phrases.aramaic: אַף יַיִן בֶּן שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים – פָּסוּל!
phrases.english: so too wine in its second year should be invalid!
And if you would say that this is indeed so,
but isn't it taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: יַיִן בֶּן שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים לֹא יָבִיא,
phrases.english: Wine in its second year one should not bring,
but if he brought it, it is valid!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה כֶּבֶשׂ בֶּן שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges חזקיה's source from Step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: חזקיה's comparison of wine to the lamb
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full comparison would make old wine completely פסול, but the ברייתא says it is כשר after the fact.

steps.title: Proof that the baraita follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the ברייתא must be רבי's, because only רבי says old wine should not be brought. That means רבי himself calls it כשר after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whom have you heard who says 'one should not bring' it? רבי. And yet he says: if he brought it, it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge by proving that the ברייתא follows רבי himself, so חזקיה's source cannot explain רבי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might answer that the ברייתא follows a different opinion. But only רבי says 'לא יביא' about old wine, so the ברייתא must be his. That means רבי holds old wine is כשר after the fact, which does not fit the lamb comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: Whom have you heard who holds this? (identifies whose opinion a source follows)

phrases.english: Whom have you heard who says "one should not bring" it?
Rabbi, and yet he says:
If he brought it, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּאָמַר לֹא יָבִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the קשיא by tying the ברייתא to רבי
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא's ruling, 'don't bring it, but if you did, it is כשר', is רבי's own view
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה, where only רבי says aged wine may not be brought

steps.title: רבא: The source is 'Do not look at wine when it is red'
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops חזקיה's source and gives a new one. The פסוק praises wine that is red, so the best wine is fresh and red.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: This is רבי's reason, as it is written: 'Do not look at wine when it is red.'
steps.whatsHappening: Because חזקיה's source failed, רבא offers a different source for רבי that fits 'don't bring it, but if you did, it is כשר'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק shows that red wine is the attractive, high-quality wine. Old wine is less red, so ideally it should not be used. But it is not disqualified, so it is כשר after the fact, which fits the ברייתא perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier approach for a new one)
This is the reason
It turns red

steps.whatToRemember: חזקיה's lamb comparison was rejected because it would make old wine completely פסול. רבא's source, red wine is the best wine, explains why רבי says old wine should not be brought but is כשר if it already was.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
This is the reason of Rabbi,
as it is written: "Do not look at wine when it is red."
phrases.notes: משלי 23:31

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces חזקיה's rejected source with a new one
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source that fits the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי learns from the lamb, which would make old wine completely פסול.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי learns from 'כי יתאדם' that red, fresh wine is best. Old wine is not ideal, but it is כשר after the fact.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a source has to match every detail of a ruling, including the difference between 'from the start' and 'after the fact'.

steps.title: Grapes from hanging vines, and what a worked vineyard means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that wine is not brought from grapes on hanging vines. A ברייתא explains that a 'worked' vineyard is one that is hoed twice a year.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one does not bring wine from grapes on hanging vines, and so on. A ברייתא taught: the good vineyards are ones that are worked twice a year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the next line of the משנה and uses a ברייתא to explain what kind of vineyard the משנה wants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה prefers wine from vineyards that are worked, over grapes hanging up high on trees or stakes. The ברייתא gives a clear measure for 'worked': the ground under the vines is hoed twice every year.

keyTerms.meaning: Vines trained up high on trees or stakes, so the grapes hang
Vineyards that are worked (the ground under them is hoed)
Twice a year

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְבִיאִין לֹא מִן הַדָּלִיּוֹת כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: One does not bring from the hanging vines, etc.
It was taught: vineyards that are worked
twice a year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aged-wine debate and moves on to the next rule in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A 'worked' vineyard, the kind the משנה prefers for wine for נסכים, is one that is hoed twice a year.

steps.title: רב יוסף's orchard and its extra-strong wine
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gave his orchard an extra hoeing, and its wine was so strong it could take twice the usual amount of water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף had a piece of an orchard. He hoed it one extra time, and it made wine that could take two measures of water for each one measure that other wine takes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story to show that extra work on a vineyard really makes better wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This backs up the ברייתא from the last step. Working the ground more often made רב יוסף's wine so strong that it needed double the normal water to be drinkable. So 'worked vineyard' in the משנה is about real quality, not just a formality.

keyTerms.meaning: An orchard
Hoeing, digging up the ground around the plants
Wine
Takes water (can be watered down)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef had
a corner of an orchard,
that he gave an extra hoeing,
and it produced wine
that took water two for one.
phrases.notes: Wine was usually mixed with water before drinking. This wine was so strong it needed double the normal amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף הֲוָה לֵיהּ קַרְנָא דְּפַרְדֵּיסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example of the ברייתא's point that working a vineyard more makes better wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Extra hoeing makes much stronger, better wine, which shows why the משנה wants wine from worked vineyards.

steps.title: Storing the wine in medium casks, not huge barrels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the wine was not stored in large barrels. A ברייתא explains that the casks used were medium-sized Lod flasks.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: they would not collect the wine into large barrels. A ברייתא taught: the casks meant here are flasks from לוד, of medium size.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה about storing the wine and uses a ברייתא to say what kind of container is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says not to store the wine in huge barrels, because that can spoil it. Instead it was kept in smaller casks. The ברייתא says exactly which ones: medium-sized flasks of the kind made in לוד.

keyTerms.meaning: Large barrels or jars for storing wine
Casks
Made in the city of לוד
Medium-sized

phrases.english: They would not collect it
into large barrels,
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which goes on to say the wine was kept in smaller casks instead.

phrases.english: It was taught: the casks are flasks
from Lod, and medium-sized.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא הָיוּ כּוֹנְסִין אוֹתָן בַּחֲצָבִין גְּדוֹלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה, about storing the wine after it is made.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine for נסכים is stored in medium-sized Lod flasks, not in large barrels.

steps.title: Setting the casks down one at a time
steps.stepSummary: Another rule is added: the casks of wine are not stacked in pairs, but each one is set down by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not set them down two by two, but rather one by one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more storage rule: each cask of wine is set down separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After saying which casks to use, the גמרא adds how to place them. They are not put one on top of another in pairs. Each cask is set down on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: Set down, place
Two by two, in pairs
One by one, each by itself

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה and ברייתות set up careful quality rules for wine for נסכים: it comes from well-worked vineyards, it is stored in medium-sized casks and not huge barrels, and each cask is set down by itself.

phrases.english: They do not set them down two by two,
phrases.notes: Meaning one cask stacked on top of another.

phrases.english: but rather one by one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a rule about how to place the casks described in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Casks of wine for נסכים are each set down separately, not stacked in pairs.

steps.title: How the treasurer checks the wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the גזבר sits with a reed and knocks when the wine starts drawing out chalky scum. A ברייתא adds that this scum comes from the sediment.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does the treasurer check the wine? He sits with a reed in his hand. When the wine starts pulling out chalky scum, he knocks with the reed. A ברייתא taught: when it pulls out the chalky scum of the sediment, the treasurer knocks with the reed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה about how the גזבר checks the wine as it pours from the cask. Then it brings a ברייתא that explains exactly when he knocks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal is to take wine only from the middle of the cask, not the dregs at the bottom. Once the wine starts bringing up chalky scum, it has reached the sediment, so the גזבר knocks to signal that the pouring should stop. The ברייתא makes clear that the chalky scum comes from the שמרים.

keyTerms.meaning: The treasurer of the בית המקדש
A reed (here used as a measuring stick and for knocking)
Chalk; here, chalk-like scum in the wine
Sediment or dregs at the bottom of the wine
He knocked or tapped

phrases.english: How does the treasurer inspect?
He sits with a reed in his hand.
If it drew out chalk, he knocks with the reed.
phrases.notes: "It" is the wine pouring out of the cask. "Chalk" means a whitish, chalky scum.

phrases.english: A baraita taught: if it drew out the chalk of the sediment,
the treasurer knocks with the reed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues going through the משנה's rules about wine for נסכים, now covering how the wine is checked.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גזבר knocks with the reed as soon as the wine starts drawing out the chalky scum of the sediment.

steps.title: Why not just say it out loud?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the גזבר knocks with a reed instead of simply telling them to stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him just say it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה: why use a reed to signal? The גזבר could just speak. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knocking seems like an extra, strange step when words would work just as well. So the גמרא asks for a reason the גזבר avoids talking.

keyTerms.meaning: To say, to speak

phrases.english: But let him just say it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the method described in the משנה quoted in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that the גזבר signals by knocking with the reed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Speaking is simpler than knocking, so why does the משנה require the reed?

steps.title: Speech is bad for wine
steps.stepSummary: The answer: this supports רבי יוחנן, who said that speech is good for spices but bad for wine. So the גזבר knocks instead of talking.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי יוחנן, for רבי יוחנן said: Just as speech is good for spices, so speech is bad for wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the גזבר stays quiet because talking harms wine. It also points out that our משנה backs up a statement of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן taught that talking helps the spices but hurts wine. The משנה's rule to knock instead of speak fits his teaching exactly. So the answer to the question also gives support to רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It supports him (his opinion)
Speech, talking
Spices

phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Yochanan,
for Rabbi Yochanan said:
Just as speech is good for spices,
phrases.notes: These are the spices of the קטורת, the incense brought in the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: so speech is bad for wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a reason for the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Knocking seems unnecessary, since speaking would work just as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: Speaking harms wine, so the גזבר signals silently with the reed. This supports רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatToRemember: The גזבר knocks instead of speaking because, as רבי יוחנן taught, speech is good for spices but bad for wine.

steps.title: Lashes for consecrating unfit wine?
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's ruling of רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה that wine with white scum is unfit, רבי יוחנן asks: if someone consecrates such wine, does he get lashes like someone who consecrates a בעל מום?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה says, etc. רבי יוחנן asked: If someone consecrated it, does he get lashes for it because of the rule against a blemished offering? Since it is unfit, is it like a blemished animal? Or perhaps the rule of a blemished offering applies only to an animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the words of רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה in the משנה and then brings a question of רבי יוחנן about it. He wants to know whether consecrating this unfit wine is punished like consecrating a blemished animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is forbidden, with lashes, to consecrate a בעל מום animal for the מזבח. The question is whether wine that is unfit counts like a 'blemished' item too. One side says anything unfit is like a בעל מום. The other side says the rule of בעל מום only applies to animals.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (raised a question he did not know the answer to)
He consecrated it (set it aside for the בית המקדש)
He receives lashes
Something with a blemish that disqualifies it as an offering
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Yehuda says, etc.
Rabbi Yochanan asked:
If one consecrated it,
what is the law, does he get lashes for it
because of the rule of a blemished offering?
Since it is unfit, is it like a blemished animal?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא אֵין בַּעַל מוּם אֶלָּא בִּבְהֵמָה?
phrases.english: Or perhaps the rule of a blemished offering applies only to an animal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה and opens a new question about it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether consecrating unfit wine brings lashes like consecrating a בעל מום animal.

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends רבי יוחנן's question with תיקו: it stays undecided.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question without an answer. Neither side is proven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no source was found to decide the question. So it is still unknown whether someone who consecrates unfit wine gets lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question stays unresolved

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רבי יוחנן's question from step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It stays undecided whether consecrating unfit wine brings lashes for בעל מום.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's question about lashes for consecrating unfit wine ends in תיקו, left unresolved.

steps.title: The best places for animals for קרבנות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists where the best animals come from: rams from מואב, lambs from חברון, calves from שרון, and young birds from הר המלך.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Rams from מואב, lambs from חברון, calves from שרון, young birds from הר המלך.
steps.whatsHappening: After finishing with flour, oil and wine, the גמרא brings a ברייתא about the best animals for קרבנות. It lists the choicest place for each type of animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the topic of bringing the finest quality to the בית המקדש. Now the focus moves from what goes into מנחות and נסכים to the animals themselves. Each kind of animal is matched with the place where the best ones are found.

keyTerms.meaning: Rams
Lambs
Calves
Young birds (doves and pigeons)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: rams from Moab,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא means the best of each kind comes from that place.

phrases.english: lambs from Hebron, calves from Sharon,
young birds from the King's Mountain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the quality of wine to the quality of animals for קרבנות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The best rams come from מואב, lambs from חברון, calves from שרון, and young birds from הר המלך.

steps.title: The best lambs are as wide as they are tall
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the lambs brought should be so fat and sturdy that their height equals their width.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: We bring lambs whose height is the same as their width.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from Step 22 continues, and רבי יהודה adds his own idea about which lambs are best.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 said where the best lambs come from (חברון). רבי יהודה adds a new point about how they should look: they should be very sturdy, as wide as they are tall.

keyTerms.meaning: Lambs
Their height is like their width; very sturdy, well-fed animals

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
We bring lambs whose height is like their width.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further opinion to the ברייתא listing the best animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the choicest lambs are as wide as they are tall.

steps.title: The source for רבי יהודה in a verse from ישעיהו
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב שילא explains that רבי יהודה learns his idea from the words כר נרחב, which can be read as 'a wide lamb'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב שילא said: What is רבי יהודה's reason? Because it is written: 'Your cattle will graze on that day in wide pastures (כר נרחב).'
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא asks what רבי יהודה's source is, then answers his own question with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כר usually means a pasture, but it can also mean a lamb. נרחב means wide. So the פסוק hints at 'a wide lamb', which supports רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? A request for the source behind a ruling
A wide pasture; here also read as 'a wide lamb'

phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Sheila said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?
As it is written: "Your cattle will graze on that day
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 30:23

phrases.english: in a wide pasture."
phrases.notes: כר can also mean a lamb, so the words hint at 'a wide lamb'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי יהודה's statement in Step 23.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that the best lambs are as wide as they are tall.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 30:23, with כר read as 'lamb' and נרחב as 'wide'.

steps.title: What do the watchmen on the walls of ירושלים say?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about watchmen on ירושלים's walls who constantly remind ה׳, and asks what they say.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'Upon your walls, ירושלים, I have set watchmen. All day and all night they will never be silent. You who remind ה׳, do not rest.' What do they say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a closing topic for the פרק. It quotes a פסוק and sets up a question: what words do these watchmen say?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the watchmen keep reminding ה׳ but does not say what they say. The גמרא asks to fill in that missing content, and the next steps will answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Your walls (the walls of ירושלים)
Watchmen, guards
Those who remind ה׳
What do they say?

phrases.english: It is written: "Upon your walls, Jerusalem, I have set watchmen;
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 62:6

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַיּוֹם וְכׇל הַלַּיְלָה תָּמִיד לֹא יֶחֱשׁוּ
phrases.english: all day and all night, they will never be silent;

phrases.aramaic: הַמַּזְכִּירִים אֶת ה׳ אַל דֳּמִי לָכֶם״.
phrases.english: you who remind the Lord, take no rest."
What do they say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new closing aggadic topic, not tied to the lambs discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The actual words the watchmen say to remind ה׳.

steps.title: They say: ה׳, have mercy on ציון
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב שילא answers that the watchmen say the פסוק 'You will arise and have mercy on ציון'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבא בר רב שילא said: They say, 'You will arise and have mercy on ציון.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer to Step 25's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The watchmen ask ה׳ to have mercy on ציון. This fits the פסוק's picture of them constantly pleading for ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: You will arise
You will have mercy on ציון

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רָבָא בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא:
phrases.english: This is what Rava bar Rav Sheila said:
"You will arise and have mercy on Zion."
phrases.notes: תהלים 102:14

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רָבָא בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The watchmen say 'אתה תקום תרחם ציון'.

steps.title: A second answer: ה׳ builds ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a different answer: the watchmen say 'ה׳ builds ירושלים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: They say, 'ה׳ builds ירושלים.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives another answer to the same question from Step 25.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the watchmen speak about ה׳ rebuilding ירושלים. Both answers are about bringing back ציון and ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: Builds ירושלים

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
"The Lord builds Jerusalem."
phrases.notes: תהלים 147:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the same question that Step 26 answered.

steps.title: What did they say before ירושלים was destroyed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the watchmen said originally, when there was no need to ask for rebuilding.
steps.simpleTranslation: And at first, what would they say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question and sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both answers so far ask for mercy and rebuilding, which only makes sense after the destruction. So the גמרא asks what the watchmen said before that, when ירושלים still stood.

keyTerms.meaning: Originally, at first
They would say

phrases.english: And at first, what would they say?
phrases.notes: He means back when ירושלים and the בית המקדש were still standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on both answers, which assume ירושלים is destroyed, and asks about the earlier time.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the watchmen said before the destruction, when there was nothing to rebuild.

steps.title: Before: ה׳ chose ציון as His home
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב שילא answers that originally the watchmen said, 'For ה׳ chose ציון; He desired it as His dwelling.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב שילא said: They would say, 'For ה׳ has chosen ציון; He desired it as His dwelling place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the follow-up question from Step 28.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the destruction there was nothing to plead for, so the watchmen praised ה׳'s choice of ציון as His home. The words change from praise to a request for rebuilding, depending on the time.

keyTerms.meaning: Chose
He desired it
As a dwelling place for Himself

steps.whatToRemember: The watchmen never stop speaking to ה׳ about ציון. When it stood, they praised His choice of it. Now they ask Him to have mercy and rebuild it.

phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Sheila said:
"For the Lord has chosen Zion;
phrases.notes: תהלים 132:13

phrases.english: He desired it as His dwelling place."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא כִּי בָחַר ה׳ בְּצִיּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 28's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Originally the watchmen said 'כי בחר ה׳ בציון אוה למושב לו'.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing כל קרבנות הציבור
steps.stepSummary: The פרק כל קרבנות הציבור ends with the Hadran formula.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק 'כל קרבנות הציבור'.
steps.whatsHappening: This line formally closes the פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Hadran is a traditional farewell said at the end of each פרק, promising to come back and learn it again. No new halacha is added here.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the closing formula of a פרק
Communal offerings; the name of this פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, "All the communal offerings."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the aggadic ending.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק כל קרבנות הציבור is complete.

steps.title: New chapter: how many dry measures were in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה states that two dry measures were in the מקדש, an עשרון and a חצי עשרון. רבי מאיר says there were three: עשרון, עשרון, and חצי עשרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: There were two measuring vessels for dry things in the מקדש: a tenth and a half-tenth. רבי מאיר says: a tenth, a tenth, and a half-tenth.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new פרק opens with a משנה that counts the dry measuring vessels in the מקדש. There is a disagreement: the תנא קמא counts two vessels, and רבי מאיר counts three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עשרון is a tenth of an איפה, the standard amount of flour for many מנחות. Both opinions agree there was one חצי עשרון. The argument is only whether there was one עשרון vessel or two.

keyTerms.meaning: Measuring vessels
Dry substances, like flour, as opposed to liquids
A tenth of an איפה; a vessel that holds that amount
Half of an עשרון; a vessel holding half a tenth
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר's 'tenth, tenth' does not mean two tenths in one vessel. It means two separate vessels, and each one holds a tenth.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Two measures
of dry substances were in the Temple:
a tenth and a half-tenth.
phrases.notes: A 'tenth' means a tenth of an איפה, a standard measure of flour.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
a tenth, a tenth, and a half-tenth.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שְׁתֵּי מִדּוֹת שֶׁל יָבֵשׁ הָיוּ בְּמִקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the Hadran in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא there were two dry measures, an עשרון and a חצי עשרון. According to רבי מאיר there were two עשרון vessels and a חצי עשרון.

steps.title: What the tenth measure was used for
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains that the עשרון was used for measuring flour for all מנחות. Even when a קרבן needed three or two tenths, they measured one tenth at a time and did not use a bigger vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was the tenth used for? With it one would measure flour for all the meal offerings. One would not measure with a three-tenth vessel for the bull, or with a two-tenth vessel for the ram. Rather, one measures them in tenths.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks, and then answers, what the עשרון vessel was used for. Its answer is that all מנחות were measured with it, one tenth at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחה that comes with a פר needs three tenths of flour, and the one that comes with an איל needs two tenths. Still, there was no three-tenth or two-tenth vessel. They filled the one-tenth vessel again and again, which explains why only small measures were needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Was used for; served
Meal offerings made from flour
A bull; its מנחה needs three tenths of flour
A ram; its מנחה needs two tenths of flour
Tenths, measured one at a time

phrases.english: The tenth, what was it used for?
With it one would measure for all the meal offerings.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיָה מוֹדֵד לֹא בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה לַפָּר
phrases.english: One would not measure with a three-tenth vessel for the bull,
phrases.notes: He means the מנחה that is brought together with a bull, which needs three tenths of flour.

phrases.english: nor with a two-tenth vessel for the ram,
rather, one measures them in tenths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the use of the first vessel listed in step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עשרון measured flour for all מנחות. Bigger amounts were measured as several single tenths, never with a larger vessel.

steps.title: What the half-tenth measure was used for
steps.stepSummary: The חצי עשרון was used to measure the flour for the חביתי כהן גדול: half in the morning and half in the afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was the half-tenth used for? With it one would measure the High Priest's griddle-cake offering: half in the morning and half in the afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the second vessel, the חצי עשרון. Its job was the daily מנחה of the כהן גדול, which is split into two halves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול brings one tenth every day, but he offers it in two parts, morning and afternoon. That is why a vessel holding exactly half a tenth was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily griddle-cake מנחה of the כהן גדול
Half
Afternoon; the time of the afternoon תמיד

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives one job to each vessel. The עשרון was for all מנחות, one tenth at a time. The חצי עשרון was for the כהן גדול's חביתין, half in the morning and half in the afternoon.

phrases.english: The half-tenth, what was it used for?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבּוֹ הָיָה מוֹדֵד חֲבִיתֵּי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
phrases.english: With it one would measure the High Priest's griddle-cake offering:
half in the morning
and half in the afternoon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 32; explains the second vessel listed in step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חצי עשרון measured the חביתי כהן גדול, half in the morning and half in the afternoon.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's source for two tenth measures
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי מאיר learns from the doubled word 'עשרון עשרון' in a פסוק that there were two עשרון vessels in the מקדש, one heaped and one leveled.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It is taught: רבי מאיר would say: Why does the פסוק say 'A tenth, a tenth, for each lamb'? This teaches that there were two tenth-measures in the מקדש, one heaped and one leveled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for רבי מאיר's opinion in the משנה. The doubled word in the פסוק shows that there were two עשרון vessels, and the ברייתא tells us how they were different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said 'עשרון' just once, so רבי מאיר reads the extra word as a hint to a second vessel. The ברייתא adds something the משנה did not say: the two vessels were not the same, since one measured a tenth when heaped and the other measured a tenth when leveled. This sets up the next explanation of what each vessel was used for.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה

steps.title: The heaped measure was used for all the meal offerings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues רבי מאיר's teaching: the heaped עשרון was the vessel used to measure flour for all the מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: With the heaped one, he would measure for all the meal offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is now explaining the job of the first of רבי מאיר's two עשרון vessels: the heaped one was used for measuring the flour of all the מנחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 34, רבי מאיר learned from the double word 'עשרון עשרון' that there were two עשרון vessels, one גדוש (heaped) and one מחוק (leveled). Here he assigns the heaped one its role: all regular מנחות were measured with it. This sets up the next piece, which will explain what the leveled one was for.
